science.title: Gap-free T2T genomic landscape of an XY male Larimichthys crocea
science.description: Larimichthys crocea (the large yellow croaker) is one of the most economically significant marine fish in East Asia. While chromosome-scale genome assemblies for three female (XX) geographical populations (Mindong, South China Sea, and Daiqu) were available, the lack of a high-quality male (XY) reference genome has hindered the exploration of male-specific sequences and the molecular mechanisms underlying sex determination. Here, we present the male T2T reference genome for the Mindong population of L. crocea by integrating Oxford Nanopore ultra-long, PacBio HiFi, and Hi-C sequencing. The assembly totals 747.28 Mb with a contig N50 of 31.79 Mb. We further achieved telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assembly and haplotype partitioning of the X and Y sex chromosomes. Telomeric repeats (TTAGGG) were identified at both termini of all 23 autosomes and two sex chromosomes. Moreover, centromeric regions exhibited significant enrichment of six major transposable elements, including DNA MULE, LTR Gypsy, DNA CMC-EnSpm, RC Helitron, LTR ERV1, and DNA TcMar-Tc2, with 76.19–93.42% of their total copies localized to centromeres. Together with a 42 bp tandem repeat (Cen-42), these elements form the centromeric architecture characterized by higher-order repeats (HORs). The T2T genome assembly exhibits high technical quality, with a BUSCO completeness of 99.6% and a base accuracy (QV) exceeding 59.75. The genome annotation yielded 29,933 protein-coding genes, providing a comprehensive map of the male-specific regions. This gap-free male reference genome provides a definitive genetic resource for studying sex-biased traits, sex chromosome evolution, and precision molecular breeding in L. crocea.

science.title: Machine learning models for the structural design of thrust active magnetic bearing and its optimization
science.description: This paper characterizes the design and structural optimization of a thrust active magnetic bearing (TAMB) that utilizes a thrust active magnet to control the rotor’s position and provide the necessary force. The magnet is designed using magnetostatic finite element analysis (FEA) in Ansys Workbench, with mesh convergence studied. Parameters that heavily influence the performance are then identified. The datasets consisting of influencing parameters and the output are generated using FEA. Two ANN models: Levenberg-Marquardt and Bayesian Regularization are trained with the help of generated datasets. Finally, TAMB is optimized by reducing the magnet volume for an axial force using PSO.

science.title: Adipic/glutamic and oxalic/glutamic-based deep eutectic solvents as potent catalysts for the green synthesis of tetrazoloquinazolinones
science.description: Two bio-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs), namely Adp/Glu-DES based on adipic acid (Adp) and glutamic acid (Glu) in a 1:1 molar ratio and Oxa/Glu-DES, composed of oxalic acid (Oxa) and Glu in a molar ratio of 3:1, were successfully prepared. The formation of both DESs was confirmed by FT-IR spectroscopy, 1H NMR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, thermal analysis, viscosity measurements, and determination of the eutectic point, demonstrating the formation of homogeneous and transparent eutectic systems. These DESs were subsequently employed as efficient and recyclable catalysts for the one-pot three-component condensation reaction of 5-aminotetrazole, dimedone, and aromatic aldehydes for the synthesis of tetrazoloquinazolinones. A wide range of substrates smoothly afforded the corresponding products under mild and environmentally benign conditions, providing good to excellent yields. Furthermore, both Oxa/Glu-DES and Adp/Glu-DES can be easily recovered and reused in multiple catalytic cycles without a significant reduction in catalytic activity, highlighting their potential as a stable and metal-free catalytic environment for the synthesis of heterocyclic compounds with medicinal value.
